content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Technical Tutorial: Feature Flags and Trunk-Based Development in Agile"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Trunk-Based Development (TBD) is a version control management practice where all developers merge their code changes into a single central branch—usually named 'main' or 'trunk'—frequently, often multiple times a day. Combined with Feature Flags, TBD enables teams to decouple deployment from release, perfectly aligning with Agile principles of continuous delivery and rapid feedback loops."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites and Core Concepts"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"A robust CI/CD pipeline capable of automated building and testing on every commit to the trunk."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"A feature flag management system (either in-house or third-party) to dynamically toggle functionality."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Discipline in writing modular code and executing short-lived branches (lasting less than a day)."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Implementing a Feature Flag in Code"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"To safely merge unfinished or experimental features into the trunk without exposing them to end-users, wrap the new code block inside a conditional check governed by a feature flag."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"if (featureFlags.isEnabled('new-checkout-flow')) { renderNewCheckout(); } else { renderLegacyCheckout(); }"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Merging Frequently to the Trunk"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Instead of working on feature branches for weeks, developers push small, incremental changes directly to the trunk multiple times a day. If a feature spans multiple days, it remains hidden behind the feature flag until it is fully ready for QA and production exposure."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 3: Managing the Lifecycle of a Feature Flag"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Technical debt associated with feature flags can accumulate if they are not cleaned up. Follow an Agile cadence to remove flags once the feature is fully rolled out and stable."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Phase 1: Create the flag and deploy code to trunk in disabled state."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Phase 2: Enable the flag for internal testing and beta users."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Phase 3: Roll out to 100% of production traffic."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Phase 4: Remove the conditional logic and the flag configuration entirely in a subsequent tech-debt sprint."},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"By uniting Trunk-Based Development with Feature Flags, Agile teams eliminate 'merge hell', accelerate deployment frequency, and reduce the risk of releasing complex software features to production."}]
